items.question: Is var dynamically typed?
items.answer: No. The compiler infers a single static type from the initializer. The Intermediate Language (IL) output is identical to writing the type name explicitly. `var` is unrelated to JavaScript `var` (scope and hoisting) and unrelated to `dynamic` (run-time binding).
followUps: Can a method parameter be declared with var?
What happens if you write var x = null without a target type?
items.sixtySeconds: `var` is compile-time inference. The type is locked after declaration. Needs an initializer. Not JS var, not dynamic.

items.question: Why use decimal for grades and money instead of double?
items.answer: `decimal` is a base-10 number type designed for exact fractional math. `double` is binary floating point — the same `0.1 + 0.2` surprise as JavaScript `number`. Use `double` for SkiaSharp transforms and sensor readings; use `decimal` for GPA, fees, and anything you print as currency.
followUps: Is string a value type or reference type?
What is the default value of bool?
items.sixtySeconds: decimal for money and grades. double for measurements and graphics. string is a reference type. bool defaults to false.

items.question: What is the difference between a value type and a reference type?
items.answer: Value type assignment copies the data (structs, enums, built-in numerics). Reference type assignment copies the reference — two variables can alias one object. Boxing wraps a value type as `object` on the heap. Do not claim structs always live on the stack; that is a Common Language Runtime (CLR) implementation detail covered in module 14.
followUps: What happens when you mutate a struct from a list indexer?
Why is string a reference type but == compares content?
items.sixtySeconds: Copy data vs alias object. Boxing for object collections. Stack/heap is CLR detail, not the language definition.

items.question: What is definite assignment?
items.answer: A compile-time rule: local variables must be assigned on every code path before their first read. Fields are zeroed automatically. `int n; Console.WriteLine(n);` fails with CS0165. Use `default`, an initializer, or assign in every branch.
followUps: Do struct locals follow the same rules?
items.sixtySeconds: Locals must be assigned on all paths. Fields default. default(int) is 0. default(string) is null.

items.question: How is int? different from a null string?
items.answer: `int?` is `Nullable<int>` — a value-type struct with `HasValue` and `Value`. A null `string` is a reference variable pointing to no object. They look similar with `??` and `?.`, but the run-time mechanisms differ. Nullable reference type annotations (`string?`) are a compiler overlay in module 07.
followUps: What happens if you call .Value on a null int??
Can you write int x = null?
items.sixtySeconds: int? is a wrapper struct. string null is a missing reference. .Value without HasValue throws.

items.question: Explain typeof, GetType, is, and as.
items.answer: `typeof(T)` returns a `System.Type` for a compile-time type name. `obj.GetType()` returns the run-time type of the instance. `is` tests compatibility and can introduce a typed variable. `as` performs a reference conversion and returns null on failure — only for reference and nullable types. `nameof` returns a string identifier, not a Type.
followUps: Why is GetType() == typeof(Base) a poor test for derived instances?
When does boxing happen with object?
items.sixtySeconds: typeof compile-time. GetType run-time. is for safe tests. as returns null on fail. nameof is a string.

items.question: When would you pick a struct over a class?
items.answer: When the data is small, copyable, and identity does not matter — coordinates, grades, timestamps. Structs copy on assignment; classes alias. Mutable structs in collections cause copy surprises. Records (class or struct) add value-based equality. Full object-oriented details are in modules 04 and 05.
followUps: Can a struct inherit from a class?
What is a record compared to a plain class?
items.sixtySeconds: Struct for small copyable data without identity. Class for lifecycle and shared mutable state. Record for equality + with.

items.question: What is the Common Type System (CTS), and how does dynamic differ from TypeScript any?
items.answer: The CTS unifies all .NET types under `object`. Value types reach `object` through boxing. `object` is statically typed — you must cast or test before using specific members. `dynamic` defers member resolution to the Dynamic Language Runtime (DLR) at run time. TypeScript `any` erases types; `unknown` forces narrowing. C# has `object` and `dynamic`, not `any` or `unknown`.
items.sixtySeconds: CTS root is object. dynamic is late binding via DLR. Not TS any. Prefer generics and typed DTOs.
